auth.description: Resend API key, sent as a bearer token on every request. Minted in the Resend dashboard and scoped there to full access or sending only; this repository holds the reference, never the value
auth.name: resend.api_key
auth.subject: unstated

description: Resend transactional email: send a message, read what happened to it, and list or inspect the domains a key may send from

operations.description: Send one email immediately. Delivered within seconds and cannot be recalled once accepted. The sending domain must already be verified on this account — resend-domain-list names the ones that are

params.description: The sending address, on a domain verified for this account. Accepts a bare address, or `Name <address>` to attach a friendly name. The caller's own input, never an example value here
params.name: from

params.description: Recipient address, or an array of up to 50 addresses. The caller's own input, never an example value here
params.name: to

params.description: The message body, as HTML. Resend generates the plain-text alternative from it, so a plain-text-only message is sent by putting the text here
params.name: html

id.description: Resend's id for this message — the argument resend-email-get takes. The only field the send answers with

operations.description: Read one sent message and its current delivery state. This is how a flow learns whether a send bounced, was delivered, or is still queued

params.description: The message's id, from resend-email-send's response
params.name: email_id

bcc.description: Blind-copied recipients — personal data, never an example value

cc.description: Copied recipients — personal data, never an example value

created_at.description: When Resend accepted the message, as a space-separated UTC timestamp rather than strict RFC 3339

from.description: The sending address used — never an example value

last_event.description: The most recent delivery event: queued, scheduled, sent, delivered, delivery_delayed, complained, bounced, or canceled. This is the field a flow branches on

message_id.description: The RFC 5322 Message-ID Resend assigned, for correlating with a recipient's own mail logs

reply_to.description: Reply-To addresses — personal data, never an example value

scheduled_at.description: When a scheduled message is due, or null for an immediate send

tags.description: The key/value metadata the send attached, if any

text.description: The plain-text alternative, or null when none was generated

to.description: The recipients this message was sent to — personal data, never an example value

operations.description: List every sending domain on this account with its verification status. Also this connector's `verify` — a bounded read that runs unattended and needs nothing configured beyond the credential

capabilities.description: Whether this domain may send and whether it may receive, each enabled or disabled

created_at.description: As a space-separated UTC timestamp rather than strict RFC 3339

id.description: The domain's id — what resend-domain-get addresses it by

name.description: The domain itself, as registered with Resend

region.description: The sending region the domain was created in, e.g. us-east-1

status.description: not_started, pending, verified, failed or temporary_failure. Only a verified domain may appear in a send's `from`

has_more.description: Whether more domains exist beyond this page. This connector declares no cursor parameters, so it reads the unpaginated default, which returns every domain

operations.description: Read one sending domain, including the DNS records it needs and the status of each. This is the diagnostic for a domain that will not verify, and therefore for a send refused with an invalid-from error

capabilities.description: Whether this domain may send and whether it may receive, each enabled or disabled

click_tracking.description: Whether Resend rewrites links to record clicks

created_at.description: As a space-separated UTC timestamp rather than strict RFC 3339

name.description: The domain itself, as registered with Resend

open_tracking.description: Whether Resend rewrites messages to record opens

records.description: The DNS records this domain needs, each with its own verification status. A domain stuck at not_started is one whose records have not been published

name.description: The record's host name, relative to the domain

priority.description: MX priority; absent on TXT and CNAME entries

record.description: Which mechanism the entry serves: SPF, DKIM or Tracking

ttl.description: Resend states this as text, e.g. "Auto", not as a number of seconds

type.description: The DNS record type: MX, TXT or CNAME

region.description: The sending region the domain was created in, e.g. us-east-1

status.description: not_started, pending, verified, failed or temporary_failure. Only a verified domain may appear in a send's `from`

tracking_subdomain.description: The subdomain link tracking is served from, when click tracking is on
